fields.sample_size: 160 households interviewed in the Nema 2 peripheral district of Ziguinchor; documentary analysis of National Agency for Demographic Statistics and SEN'EAU data; interviews with SEN'EAU and municipal actors
fields.effect_estimate: Production capacity of 9,500 m3/day (400 m3/h) is below demand from an estimated 583,528 inhabitants, with the deficit concentrated in peripheral districts such as Nema 2; the household survey (160 households) shows water is not effectively available in sufficient quantity there; causes given are inadequate and abandoned infrastructure, pollution and salinity of water resources, and poor governance of the supply sector (limited household involvement in management). Descriptive.
fields.study_design: mixed-methods case study of one peripheral district (documentary analysis, 160-household survey, interviews)
fields.section: Full text: Methodology (three axes: documentary research, data collection, data processing); Results and discussion (household survey, involvement in water management); Conclusion
fields.exact_location: Methodology (three axes: documentary research, data collection, data processing); Results and discussion (household survey, involvement in water management); Conclusion

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a household survey (160 households) and documentary analysis of drinking-water supply in Nema 2, Ziguinchor, Senegal, read in full text 2026-10-04. Supply capacity falls short of demand; causes are infrastructure, pollution and salinity, and poor governance; households are little involved in management. Descriptive.
